nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of Ni3Se2/FeSe2, Ni3Se2, FeSe2
nodes.procedure: Ni3Se2/FeSe2 nanosheets, Ni3Se2, and FeSe2 were synthesized by the same facile hydrothermal method. For Ni3Se2/FeSe2: nickel foam and Fe(NO3)3·9H2O were used. For Ru-FeSe2 synthesis, only Fe(NO3)3·9H2O was incorporated. For Ru-Ni3Se2 synthesis, only nickel foam was introduced.
nodes.source_text: First, the Ni3Se2/FeSe2 nanosheets were synthesized by a facile hydrothermal method. ... the contrast samples, including Ni3Se2/FeSe2, Ni3Se2, and FeSe2, were also synthesized by the same hydrothermal method.

nodes.name: Ru electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Then, the Ru-Ni3Se2/FeSe2 catalyst was obtained by an electrodeposition process. Under the condition of electric field, Ru atoms in aqueous solution were uniformly anchored on the Ni3Se2/FeSe2 support.
nodes.source_text: Then, the Ru-Ni3Se2/FeSe2 catalyst was obtained by an electrodeposition process. Under the condition of electric field, Ru atoms in aqueous solution were uniformly anchored on the support.

nodes.description: HER performance evaluation in 1.0 M KOH three-electrode cell
nodes.source_text: The HER activities ... were systematically evaluated by a standard three-electrode cell configuration in 1_M KOH as the electrolyte. The Ru - N i_{3}S e_{2} / Fe S e_{2} just requires an overpotential of 43 mV to reach a current density of 10 mA cm^{-2} ... Tafel slopes ... are 87 ... mV dec^{-1} ... exhibits the smallest charge transfer resistance (R_ct) ... mass activity of 3593.61 mA mg^{-1} at 200 mV overpotential ... C_dl value of the Ru - Ni_3Se_2 / FeSe_2 (21.40 mF cm^{-2}) ... no significant degradation is observed after 40 hours test

nodes.evidence_snippet: The diffraction peaks in the XRD pattern of Ru - N_i_3Se_2 / FeSe_2 catalyst correspond to the standard PDF cards of Ni_3Se_2 (PDF #19-0841) and FeSe_2 (PDF #21-0432). The distinctive characteristic peaks at 20.93°, 29.55°, 29.97°, 42.63°, 48.21°, 52.74°, 53.74°, 62.30°, 70.47°, and 85.19° correspond to the (101), (110), (012), (202), (122), (300), (104), (024), (214), and (232) crystal planes of Ni_3Se_2, respectively. Meanwhile, the characteristic peaks at 30.87°, 34.91°, and 54.05° are attributed to the (020), (111), and (031) crystal planes of FeSe_2. However, no characteristic peak of Ru particles is observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru content in Ru-Ni3Se2/FeSe2 catalyst is 0.4%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The results show the content of Ru in the catalyst is only 0.4%.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-Ni3Se2/FeSe2 and Ni3Se2/FeSe2 catalysts exhibit nanosheet structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images confirm the Ru - N_i_3Se_2 / FeSe_2 and Ni_3Se_2 / FeSe_2 catalysts exhibit nanosheet structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED of Ru-Ni3Se2/FeSe2 reveals (121) plane of FeSe2 and (003) plane of Ni3Se2; HRTEM shows abundant Ni3Se2/FeSe2 interface; inverse FFT confirms 0.246 nm (021) Ni3Se2 and 0.247 nm (120) FeSe2 lattice spacings.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) image of Ru - N_i_3Se_2 / FeSe_2 presented in Figure 1b reveals the existence of (121) plane of FeSe_2 and (003) plane of Ni_3Se_2. As shown in the HRTEM image in Figure 1c, there is an abundant Ni_3Se_2 / FeSe_2 interface for Ru - N_i_3Se_2 / FeSe_2. Inverse Fourier transform image reveals the lattice stripe with a spacing of 0.246 nm is indexed to the (021) crystal plane of Ni_3Se_2 and the interplanar distance of 0.247 nm is attributed to the (120) crystal plane of FeSe_2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Bright spots identified as uniformly dispersed Ru single atoms on Ru-Ni3Se2/FeSe2 surface, enriched at Ni3Se2/FeSe2 interface; line profiles confirm single atoms, no Ru clusters.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As illustrated in Figure 1f, spherical aberration corrected high-angle annular dark-field-scanning transmission election microscopy (AC-HAADF-STEM) was performed to identify the Ru single atoms... the bright spots in Figure 1f (highlighted in red circles) are identified as Ru single atoms.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru, Ni, Fe, Se, O elements uniformly distributed on Ru-Ni3Se2/FeSe2 catalyst surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The AC-HAADF-STEM image and the corresponding energy dispersive spectrometer (EDS) element mapping images show that the Ru, Ni, Fe, Se, and O elements are uniformly distributed on the catalyst surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-Ni3Se2/FeSe2 XPS shows Ni2+ at 855.27/873.18 eV, Ni0 at 851.97/869.08 eV; Fe3+ at 709.86/722.66 eV, Fe2+ at 705.54/718.34 eV; Se-M at 53.95/54.48 eV, Se-O at 58.58 eV; Ru 3d5/2 at 280.00 eV, 3d3/2 at 284.73 eV; binding energy shifts indicate electron transfer from Ru to Ni3Se2/FeSe2 interface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2a displays the peaks at 855.27 and 873.18 eV for the Ru - N i_{3}S e_{2} / F e S e_{2} are assigned to the Ni^{2 + }. Meanwhile, the peaks at the binding energies of 851.97 and 869.08 eV correspond to the Ni^0 ... the main peaks at 709.86 and 722.66 eV are attributed to the Fe^{3+} species ... two peaks at 53.95 and 54.48 eV belong to the Se 3d_{5/2} and Se 3d_{3/2} ... the peak located at the binding energy of 58.58 eV can be ascribed to the Se-O ... the peaks centered at 280.00 and 284.73 eV are assigned to Ru 3d_{5/2} and Ru 3d_{3/2} signals.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES positions Ru-Ni3Se2/FeSe2 between Ru foil and RuO2 (valence +2.73); FT-EXAFS shows Ru-O coordination at 1.6 Å (CN=3), Ru-Se at 1.9 Å (CN=2) and 2.1 Å (CN=2); no Ru-Ru bonds confirm single atom dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The position of the absorption edge of Ru in Ru - N_i_3Se_2 / FeSe_2 is located between Ru foil and RuO_2. This indicates that the Ru atoms exist in the oxidation state, and the valence of Ru is +2.73 ... the Ru element in Ru - N_i_3Se_2 / FeSe_2 exhibits three distinct coordination peaks ... coordination peak at 1.6 Å and the corresponding coordination number of Ru-O is 3 ... coordination peak at 1.9 Å is attributed to Ru-Se with a coordination number of 2, while the peak at 2.1 Å is also assigned to the Ru-Se bond with a coordination number of 2 ... no Ru-Ru bonds is found in Ru - N_i_3Se_2 / FeSe_2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-Ni3Se2/FeSe2: 4.47 m²/g; Ni3Se2/FeSe2: 5.39 m²/g; FeSe2: 3.56 m²/g; Ni3Se2: 4.20 m²/g; all show typical H3 hysteresis loop.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The specific surface areas of Ru - N i_{3}Se_{2} / FeSe_{2} , Ni_{3}Se_{2} / FeSe_{2} , FeSe_{2} , and Ni_{3}Se_{2} are 4.47 m^2 / g , 5.39 m^2 / g , 3.56 m^2 / g , and 4.20 m^2 / g , respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-Ni3Se2/FeSe2 under HER shows Ru-OH peaks at 472 cm⁻¹, 556 cm⁻¹ increasing with potential; under OER shows Ru-O at 430, 497, 605 cm⁻¹ and Ru-OOH at 798 cm⁻¹ confirming H* and OOH* adsorption at Ru sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For HER, the characteristic peaks at 472 cm^{-1} and 556 cm^{-1} are attributed to the Ru-OH bonds ... in situ Raman spectroscopy reveals that the distinctive peaks at 430, 497, and 605 cm^{-1} are ascribed to the Ru-O. Notably, the peak at 798 cm^{-1} is attributed to Ru-OOH.
